subject: Intermittent on-prem DB sessions — suspected MTU/PMTU blockage at customer edge
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@bluearc.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@bluearc.health>
Date: 2027-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange hang to on-prem DB from private deployment

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for jumping on this. Over the last 24 hours our App team has intermittently seen TCP sessions to the on-prem Postgres DB in their VPC hang during connection setup. Server side we see SYNs from the Redwood private deployment reach the DB host, but the client-side never completes the handshake (no ACK to server SYN-ACK).

We captured a short pcap from the customer edge during a failed connect and attached a tiny text export (pcap_snippet.txt). The pattern looks like SYN -> SYN-ACK -> (no ACK). When we force a 1200 MTU on the client side everything works, which points at a PMTU/MTU path issue somewhere between Redwood private egress and our firewall/handoff.

We host the private deployment in our on-prem colocation and the customer peer is a managed firewall. Could you advise what checks you want from our side and whether Redwood can run any quick diagnostics from the private control plane?

We’re on US-PST. Available windows for a quick troubleshooting window today: 11:30–12:30 or 16:00–17:30.

Thanks —
Marta
Network Engineer, BlueArc Health
(attachment: pcap_snippet.txt)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@bluearc.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange hang to on-prem DB from private deployment

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the pcap and clear reproduction notes. Appreciate you surfacing the forced-1200 MTU test — that’s a strong PMTU signal. I’ve looped in Networking (Karthik) and Private Deployments (Vanessa).

Immediate asks from Redwood to help us scope:
- Can you paste the edge firewall model and ACLs that touch PMTU/ICMP (or confirm if ICMP blackholing is in place)?
- Can you run traceroute --mtu (or tracepath) from the customer side toward the DB VIP and attach results?
- On the Redwood side I’ll check the private egress path and NAT behavior for that tenant; can you confirm the tenant ID + DB VIP?

Proposed short plan for later today: 16:00 PDT troubleshooting window (we’ll be ready to toggle MSS clamp/PMTU passthrough at the edge). If we see PMTUD probes dropped we’ll coordinate a firewall rule change and temporary MSS clamp on the Redwood side to restore connections while the customer updates their appliance.

Will stand up a quick mutual action plan and escalate to on-call infra if we need a change window.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta@bluearc.health>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange hang to on-prem DB from private deployment

Evelyn / team —

I looked at the pcap quickly. A few notes and a short checklist (attachment: playbook-checklist.md).

Observations from pcap_snippet:
- We see SYN from Redwood egress -> Customer firewall -> DB host. DB replies with SYN-ACK. The SYN-ACK gets fragmented by an intermediate device (SYN-ACK with DF=0 and an 1500->... fragment). The client never sends ACK.
- Classic PMTUD failure pattern: large TCP handshake segment hits smaller MTU and ICMP needed to inform sender is being dropped by the firewall or an upstream middlebox.

Hypotheses to validate in parallel:
1) Customer edge firewall is blocking inbound ICMP (type 3 code 4) or dropping ICMP on certain routes.
2) There is a NAT hairpin / conntrack asymmetry causing the outbound SYN to be NATed differently than the SYN-ACK return (conntrack drop on return).
3) MSS clamping not applied on the path; enabling MSS clamp on either side can be a short-term mitigation.

Playbook (short):
- Customer: run tracepath/tracehops with MTU probe toward DB VIP and capture firewall syslog during a failed attempt.
- Redwood (me): confirm NAT mapping and conntrack counts for that tenant on our private gateway; enable temporary logging for conntrack drops.
- Temporary mitigation: coordinate a 15-minute change window to add an allow for ICMP type 3 or apply MSS clamp (e.g., 1360) on the customer-facing interface.

If the customer firewall policy is managed by a 3rd party (managed service), we’ll need contact info & ticket link. I’ve attached a concise checklist (playbook-checklist.md) with exact commands to run and what logs to capture.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: playbook-checklist.md)
From: Marta Lopez <marta@bluearc.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@bluearc.health>, BlueArc Health NOC <noc@bluearc.health>
Date: 2027-09-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange hang to on-prem DB from private deployment

Karthik / Evelyn —

Quick update from our run at 14:30 PDT: tracepath shows the MTU drops at the managed firewall hop; our managed service confirms they intentionally block some ICMP types by default. We pushed a limited rule to allow "ICMP fragmentation needed" (type 3 code 4) for the DB VIP and re-ran. After that the tracepath completed and a connection test succeeded.

We still want Redwood to enable the temporary MSS clamp on your private gateway as a safety net during the customer firewall rollout. Our Managed Service will schedule a permanent policy exception later this week, but they will only approve it after Redwood confirms the temporary change won’t cause other issues.

We can do a coordinated 15-minute window at 16:00 PDT today. Please confirm the exact command you'll run and your rollback steps.

Thanks —
Marta
(attachment: none)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@bluearc.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange hang to on-prem DB from private deployment — Scheduled mitigation and follow-up

Thanks everyone —

We will proceed with the coordinated 15-minute mitigation window at 16:00 PDT (started and completed). Summary of actions taken by Redwood during the window: 16:00–16:15 PDT
- Enabled MSS clamp 1360 on the tenant-facing private gateway (command: netsh nm mss-clamp set 1360 on interface tenant-42) [note: we used the platform-equivalent; actual command logged in change ticket].
- Enabled short-term conntrack debug for tenant-42; no abnormal conntrack asymmetry observed during the test after MSS clamp.
- Verified successful TCP handshake for multiple app clients to DB VIP; no packet loss in 5-minute synthetic test.

Customer actions: BlueArc allowed ICMP type 3/code 4 for the DB VIP and will schedule a permanent policy update this week.

Next steps / follow-up:
- BlueArc to confirm permanent firewall rule change and provide change ticket id.
- Redwood will keep MSS clamp in place for 24 hours as a safety net and then remove if no regressions are observed.
- Karthik to file a small postmortem with exact pcap excerpts and recommended guardrails for future private handoffs (JIRA NETOPS-4621).

Thanks for the quick coordination. If any part of the rollback window causes issues, ping the private-deploy-onsite channel and I’ll escalate to infra on-call.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: firewall-rule-change-req.pdf)
